data.title: Nvidia, Intel, Tesla, AMD, Coherent, Lam Research, Moderna, and More Stocks That Explain Today's Market — Barrons.com
data.description:
By George Glover, Kit Norton and Ty Roush

Stocks rose Friday as many artificial-intelligence-related stocks recovered from the previous session's brutal selloff and as Wall Street digested a better-than-expected U.S. jobs report.

Intel gained 7.2%, having slumped 50% over the past month because of disappointing third-quarter results.

Nvidia rose 3.5%. Investors appeared to be buying the dip after the chip maker's stock recorded its second largest one-day market cap decline on record on Thursday.

Coherent rose 12% and was the best-performing stock in the S&P 500 for the trading session. It fell 13% on Thursday. Advanced Micro Devices, was also one of the best-performing components, advancing 9.5% after tumbling 17% on Thursday.

Memory-card supplier Sandisk rose 4.1% after dropping 22% in the previous session. Dell, Micron, and Lumentum each gained more than 4%.

Lam Research rose 9.1%. The chip tool maker said its board had approved $25 billion in share buybacks and a quarterly dividend of 33 cents a common stock.

Iren gained 20%. The AI cloud computing company reported better-than-expected revenue in the fiscal first quarter. Iren said that its AI cloud revenue in the quarter increased 182% sequentially.

Tesla rose 4.5%. CEO Elon Musk said the company would wind down Cybertruck production next year.

Airbnb rose 11.2%. The vacation rental site posted strong third-quarter results and raised its full-year outlook, citing strong travel demand. "Airbnb is back in growth mode," the company said in a letter to shareholders.

Cloudflare advanced 12%. The cybersecurity company reported a 39% surge in third-quarter revenue and raised its guidance, helping shares rally after they slumped 8% in Thursday's tech selloff.

Quantum computing company IonQ posted strong quarterly earnings as revenue more than quadrupled to $173.8 million. The stock advanced 16%.

JFrog surged 35% after the software company posted blowout third-quarter earnings that gave management the confidence to bump up its full-year guidance on the back of AI coding demand.

Biotech company Moderna surpassed Wall Street expectations with its third-quarter earnings. Moderna stock rose 9.1%.

AST SpaceMobile rose 6.8% after the aerospace company announced plans to build its own reusable rocket. Shares of rocket engine partner Firefly Aerospace surged 31%.

Atlassian sank 15% as investors appeared concerned about the software company's slowing cloud revenue growth. Analysts argued the selloff was unwarranted.

DraftKings tumbled 27%. The sports gambling company cut its earnings and revenue outlook for 2026 as it pours more money into growing its prediction markets business.

Axon Enterprise dropped 18% and was the worst performer in the S&P 500 for the session. The Taser maker missed expectations with its third-quarter earnings and cut its full-year guidance after stalled federal deployments of the company's AI-powered counter-drone platform.

Write to George Glover at george.glover@dowjones.com, Kit Norton at kit.norton@barrons.com and Ty Roush at tyler.roush@barrons.com

data.description:
Santander Holdings USA, Inc. (“SHUSA”) today announced that its Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $328.125 per share ($0.328125 per each depositary share (the “Depositary Shares”), NYSE: SNUS PF H, CUSIP 80282 K700, 1,000 of which represents one preferred share) on its Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series H (“Series H Preferred Stock”), payable December 15, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 30, 2026.

SHUSA also announced that, on December 15, 2026, it will redeem all 6,000 outstanding shares of its Series H Preferred Stock, and the corresponding 6,000,000 Depositary Shares. The Depositary Shares will be redeemed at a redemption price of $25.00 per Depositary Share.

The redemption price does not include the regular quarterly dividend that was declared and will be paid in the customary manner.

The Depositary Shares are held in book-entry form through the Depository Trust Company (“DTC”) and will be redeemed in accordance with the procedures of DTC. Payment to DTC for the Depositary Shares will be made by Broadridge Corporate Issuer Solutions, LLC as redemption agent. The address for Broadridge Corporate Issuer Solutions, LLC is 51 Mercedes Way, Edgewood, NY 11717, Attention: President.

About SHUSA

SHUSA is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Madrid-based Banco Santander, S.A. () (“Santander”), recognized as one of the world’s most admired companies by Fortune Magazine in 2026, with more than 182 million customers in the United States, Europe and Latin America. SHUSA is the intermediate holding company for Santander’s five growing businesses in the United States. Santander’s U.S. presence consists of auto lending, retail and digital banking, commercial banking, corporate and investment banking, and wealth management businesses. data.title: Copper One Completes Second Hole of 2026 Phase 2 Drill Program (MHB-40) at Flagship Majuba Hill Project, Nevada
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Vancouver, BC – November 6, 2026 – TheNewswire - Copper One Resources Corp. (“Copper One”) (CSE: CEXY | OTCID: CEXYF | FSE: IW8 | WKN: A42AGR) (the “Company”) announces the completion of drill hole MHB-40, the second hole of its 2026 Phase 2 diamond drilling program of up to 10,000 feet at its 100%-owned flagship Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project (“Majuba Hill” or the “Project”) in Pershing County, Nevada.

MHB-40 reached a final downhole depth of 1,615 feet (492 metres). Preliminary core logging identified possible porphyry D-type veins associated with pervasive phyllic alteration characterized by quartz, sericite and pyrite.

MHB-40 Highlights

  • Hole orientation: MHB-40 was drilled on an azimuth of 030° at an inclination of −55°.

  • Veining and alteration: Core logging identified possible D-type veins associated with pervasive quartz-sericite-pyrite alteration.

  • Phase 2 drilling to date: MHB-40 and the previously completed MHB-39 account for a combined 3,075 feet (937 metres) of diamond drilling.

David Greenway, President and Chief Executive Officer of Copper One, commented: “We’re advancing copper exploration across our North American portfolio, with drilling at Majuba Hill in Nevada and Redonda in British Columbia. New copper supply takes years to develop, and the work we do today helps us decide which targets warrant further drilling. At Majuba Hill, we continue to see encouraging features in our Phase 2 drill core. Our geologists observed native copper and copper oxides in MHB-39, followed by possible porphyry D-type veins associated with quartz-sericite-pyrite alteration in MHB-40. We’re evaluating whether those veins mark an upper level of the porphyry system and could help guide deeper drilling.”

Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 1: Visually identified sulfides (pyrite with chalcopyrite) associated with stockwork veins and pervasive quartz-sericite-pyrite alteration. Visual identification is preliminary and should not be considered a substitute for laboratory assay results.

The Company’s expanded Phase 2 diamond core drilling program (the “Phase 2 Program”) comprises up to 10,000 feet (3,048 metres) of HQ/PQ diamond core drilling. The Phase 2 Program is intended to accelerate systematic testing of priority targets at Majuba Hill and support the Company’s objective of advancing the Project toward an inaugural mineral resource estimate prepared in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”). More than 95,000 feet (28,956 metres) have been drilled to date at Majuba Hill across more than 100 drill holes.

Phase 2 Program Highlights

  • Expanded program of up to 10,000 feet (3,048 metres) of diamond core drilling.


  • An initial drilling scope of approximately 5,000 feet (1,524 metres) contracted to Evolve using one portable HQ/PQ core drill.


  • Continuous, two-shift drilling operations planned 24 hours a day, seven days a week.


  • Maximum planned hole depth under the initial scope of approximately 1,700 feet (518 metres), with final collar locations, azimuths, inclinations and depths to be determined by the Company’s technical team.


  • Real-time operational visibility through Evolve’s EVX Connect platform.


Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 2: Fine-grained pyrite and minor chalcopyrite associated with possible porphyry-related veins. Visual identification is preliminary and should not be considered a substitute for laboratory assay results.

Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 3: Previously published view of drill pad 26DPH-8 at Copper One Resources Corp.’s 100%-owned Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project in Pershing County, Nevada.

Real-Time Drill Program Technology

As previously announced, the Company engaged Evolve Exploration Nevada, LLC (“Evolve”) to undertake the Phase 2 diamond core drilling.

Every Evolve drill rig operates on EVX Connect, Evolve’s real-time operational platform. Through EVX Connect, Copper One expects to receive live drilling metrics, digital PLOD reporting, drill-hole coordinate tracking, streamlined invoicing and high-quality photographs of drill core as it is recovered. Information will be accessible through web and mobile interfaces, providing the Company’s technical and management teams with timely visibility into drilling progress and field operations.

About the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project, Nevada

Majuba Hill is Copper One Resources Corp.’s flagship copper-silver-gold exploration project, located in Pershing County, Nevada, USA. Nevada ranked first globally on the Investment Attractiveness Index in the Fraser Institute’s Annual Survey of Mining Companies 2025. The property comprises approximately 9,684 acres (3,919 hectares) and is situated approximately 70 miles (113 road kilometres) southwest of Winnemucca and 156 miles (251 kilometres) northeast of Reno.

The project benefits from excellent infrastructure, including year-round road access, nearby electrical power and water, and access to a skilled mining workforce. Majuba Hill is a past-producing copper mine with an extensive exploration database, including records from historical and recent drilling programs, providing a strong technical foundation for ongoing exploration aimed at further defining the extent and economic potential of the mineralized system.

Exploration has outlined a large copper-silver-gold hydrothermal mineralized system that remains open for expansion. Current exploration is focused on advancing the Company's geological model through systematic drilling, geological mapping, geochemical sampling, and structural interpretation to evaluate the scale, continuity, and significance of mineralization. Additional drilling and technical studies will be required to further define the extent and economic potential of the mineralized system.

Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Larry Segerstrom, M.Sc. (Geology), CPG, a non-independent consulting geologist to the Company and a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.

About Copper One Resources Corp.

Copper One Resources Corp. is focused on identifying, acquiring and advancing high-potential copper, copper-silver-gold and copper-molybdenum projects to help meet global demand for critical metals used in electrification, AI infrastructure and data centres, renewable energy, defence and power system modernization.

The Company's flagship asset is the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold District, located approximately 156 miles (251 kilometres) from Reno, Nevada. Majuba Hill is an exploration-stage porphyry copper project situated in an established mining jurisdiction with existing infrastructure, where ongoing exploration is focused on evaluating the scale and continuity of a copper-silver-gold mineralized system.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Redonda Copper-Molybdenum Project, located northeast of Campbell River in British Columbia's Vancouver Mining Division. The district-scale project comprises approximately 2,746.46 hectares (6,786 acres) across nine mineral claims and hosts a porphyry-style copper-molybdenum system within the Coast Suture Zone, a geological belt known for porphyry copper and skarn mineralization. Systematic exploration is continuing to evaluate the scale and continuity of the mineralized system.

In addition, Copper One holds an option to earn up to a 100% interest in the Redhill Property, located south of Ashcroft, British Columbia, adjacent to the Trans-Canada Highway. The 4,736-hectare (11,704-acre) property hosts volcanogenic massive sulfide (VMS) mineralization prospective for copper, zinc, silver and gold, while also demonstrating potential for epithermal gold mineralization.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Sport Project in Utah through its wholly owned subsidiary, Rooinek Mining Corp., expanding the Company’s portfolio of North American copper exploration assets.

Copper One is advancing its portfolio through systematic exploration, modern geological modelling and disciplined technical evaluation. The Company remains committed to responsible exploration practices, technical transparency and the disciplined advancement of critical-metals projects across North America.

All stakeholders are encouraged to follow the Company on its social media profiles on LinkedIn and X.com, and to subscribe for updates at https://copperone.com/.

data.title: Tech-Heavy Nasdaq Regains Ground But Dow Sees Further Downside
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Following the sell-off seen during Thursday's session, stocks moved back to the upside during trading on Friday. The tech-heavy Nasdaq showed a notable rebound, although the Dow saw continued weakness.

The major averages ended the day mixed. While the Dow fell 237.33 points or 0.5 percent to 51,285.73, the S&P 500 rose 23.13 points or 0.3 percent to 7,376.86 and the Nasdaq jumped 264.43 points or 1.1 percent to 24,579.42.

For the week, the Nasdaq plunged by 3.4 percent, the S&P 500 tumbled by 2.7 percent and the Dow slid by 0.9 percent.

The rebound on Wall Street largely reflected bargain hunting following the substantial pullback seen during Thursday's session.

The tech-led sell-off dragged the Nasdaq down to its lowest closing level in over six months, while the S&P 500 plunged to a three-month closing low.

Semiconductor stocks have helped lead the way back to the upside, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index spiking by 4.2 percent following the 12.3 percent nosedive seen on Thursday.

Substantial strength was also visible among networking stock, as reflected by the 4.1 percent surge by the NYSE Arca Networking Index.

Outside of the tech sector, gold stocks moved sharply higher despite a decrease by the price of the precious metal, driving the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index up by 2.6 percent.

Airline and oil service stocks also saw considerable strength on the day, while housing stocks showed a notable move to the downside.

In U.S. economic news, a closely watched report released by the Labor Department showed employment in the U.S. increased by far more than anticipated in the month of October.

The Labor Department said non-farm payroll employment jumped by 165,000 jobs in October compared to economist estimates for the addition of 62,000 jobs.

The report also showed employment surged by an upwardly revised 186,000 jobs in August and climbed by an upwardly revised 60,000 jobs in September, reflecting a net upward revision of 84,000 jobs.

The report also said the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1 percent in October from 4.2 percent in September. The unemployment rate was expected to remain unchanged.

'The latest jobs data suggest labor market conditions are tightening, and with inflation well above target, that adds to the case for a December rate hike,' said Michael Pearce, Chief U.S. Economist at Oxford Economics.

He added, 'However, given most of the core inflation overshoot we expect is tied to spillovers from higher energy prices and AI-related pressures, continued falls in tech stocks and oil prices could eliminate the prospect of an additional hike in early 2027.'

Meanwhile, preliminary data released by the University of Michigan showed an unexpected improvement in U.S. consumer sentiment in the month of November.

The University of Michigan said its consumer sentiment index rose to 51.0 in November from 48.0 in October. Economists had expected the index to remain unchanged.

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved sharply lower during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index plunged by 6 percent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index slumped by 1.1 percent.

The major European markets also showed notable moves to the downside. The German DAX Index tumbled by 1.9 percent, the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index slid by 1 percent and the French CAC 40 Index fell by 0.8 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries saw modest weakness after trending higher over the past several sessions. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, rose 2.2 basis points to 4.859 percent.

data.title: Update - Brookfield Revels in Rising Demand for Infrastructure Assets — WSJ
data.description:
By Luis Garcia and Robb M. Stewart

Brookfield Asset Management expects its infrastructure investment strategy to propel operations into next year as investors see such assets providing some immunity to market volatility and a shield to inflation.

Capital has poured into the New York firm's latest main infrastructure fund, with $26 billion collected for the vehicle so far, including $3.4 billion during this year's third quarter and $13 billion received after the end of September.

"This is going to be the largest fund in the history of Brookfield," Chief Executive Connor Teskey said Friday during a call with securities analysts to discuss the firm's third-quarter results. He added that the fund is expected to surpass a $30 billion goal by early next year.

Brookfield raised roughly $25 billion during the just-ended quarter across all its strategies and amassed $123 billion in fresh capital this year through September. The firm with roots in Canada continues to benefit from investors' appetite for infrastructure assets.

"Economic uncertainty, volatile public markets and the prospect of higher inflation" are driving investors to the strategy, said Rene Lubianski, a managing partner in the firm's infrastructure group who spoke on the call.

"[Infrastructure] provides essential services with durable demand, often supported by long-term contracts or regulated frameworks" that typically include price adjustments based on inflation, Lubianski said of such assets. "Together, these characteristics provide downside protection, predictable cash flow, consistent growth through market cycles and meaningful diversification."

The rising demand for physical assets to support the expansion of digital technologies, the repatriation of manufacturing and the shift to clean energy are all drawing investors to infrastructure strategies, Brookfield executives said during the call, referring to the three trends as digitalization, deglobalization and decarbonization.

Earlier this week, Brookfield said it partnered with power company Drax in the U.K. to build an artificial intelligence computing facility in North England, an investment that could exceed GBP20 billion, equivalent to $26.9 billion. Other recent investments in the sector include the firm's pledge in July to provide as much as $9 billion in financing to expand AI-computing power at data centers in South Korea. Major AI chip maker Nvidia is investing $1 billion in Korean data-center operator Naver.

"Together with the opportunities we're advancing in the United States, Canada and Europe, these projects demonstrate the scale, geographic breadth and quality of the pipeline behind the strategy," Lubianski said.

During the third quarter, Brookfield raised $12.2 billion for credit strategies, $2.1 billion for private-equity funds, $2.3 billion for energy-focused vehicles and $900 million for real-estate investment pools. The firm, whose ultimate parent is Toronto-based Brookfield Corp., ended September with assets of roughly $1.3 trillion.

Regarding potential fallout on the AI industry from the U.S. midterm elections, Teskey said it's too early to assess all the ramifications, noting only that a Democratic majority in Congress could lead to changes in project permitting processes and another extension of renewable energy tax credits, which are set to expire next year.

"We're not banking on that in any way, but should either of those things take place, it would be a very strong positive for our business," he said.

Brookfield notched a 15% gain in distributable earnings, a measure of cash that can be returned to shareholders, which rose to $763 million, or 47 cents a share, from $661 million, or 41 cents in the year-ago period. Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting $735 million, or about 45 cents a share.

Fee-related earnings also climbed 15% to $864 million for the just-ended quarter compared with the year-earlier period, topping the almost $835 million analysts anticipated, according to FactSet.

Revenue jumped 72% to $2.15 billion.

Capital inflows and deployment helped drive a more than threefold increase in net income, which rose to $2.65 billion, or $1.64 cents a share, for the third quarter.

Brookfield shares were little changed in early afternoon trading Friday following release of the results.

data.title: Peter Kolchinsky and Rajeev Shah Disclose 14.6% Stake in Bambusa Therapeutics
data.description:
Peter Kolchinsky and Rajeev Shah Disclose 14.6% Stake in Bambusa Therapeutics

Peter Kolchinsky and Rajeev Shah, who control RA Capital Management, L.P., disclosed beneficial ownership of 7,429,758 shares of Bambusa Therapeutics, Inc., equal to 14.6% of its common stock. Their Schedule 13D, dated Nov. 6, 2026, followed Bambusa’s Nov. 2 IPO and disclosed open-market purchases by the Fund on Oct. 30. The investors say they bought the shares for investment, not to change control, but may discuss Bambusa’s strategy and governance.

Investor Intent

The investors say they have no current plans to pursue changes covered by Schedule 13D’s specified actions. They may talk with Bambusa leaders, directors, shareholders and other parties about its operations, strategic direction, governance, capitalization, or possible business combinations and dispositions. RA Capital partner Derek DiRocco already serves on Bambusa’s board and will take part in regular board and management discussions as a director.

Investor's Background

RA Capital Management, L.P. provides investment management services to RA Capital Healthcare Fund, L.P. and RA Capital Nexus Fund III, L.P. Peter Kolchinsky and Rajeev Shah control the general partner of RA Capital and may be treated as beneficial owners of securities managed by the firm. RA Capital Healthcare Fund is a private investment vehicle, and RA Capital directs voting and investment decisions for the shares reported in this filing.
